    Göbel–Simson rigid families (Theorem 5.6) #

    For an infinite field k and an infinite type X of cardinality κ there are Kronecker modules T_β = (V_β, W_β; a_β, b_β), β ⊆ X, with dim V_β = dim W_β = κ, a_β, b_β injective and a_β(V_β) + b_β(V_β) = W_β, such that Hom(T_β, T_γ) ≅ k for β ⊆ γ, Hom(T_β, T_γ) = 0 for β ⊄ γ, and End(T_β) ≅ k as k-algebras (Bricks.rigidFamily). This is the form of Göbel and Simson's Theorem 1.2 and Theorem 3.3 recorded as Theorem 5.6 of the manuscript, here for infinite fields.

    The proof glues: take an anchored family over X ⊕ X (Bricks.exists_anchored) and let T_β be the module glued from the constituents indexed by inl '' β ∪ range inr. Every map T_β → T_γ is a scalar multiple of the inclusion for β ⊆ γ (Bricks.hom_subExt_of_subset) and vanishes otherwise (Bricks.hom_subExt_eq_zero); the copies indexed by range inr give the dimension κ.

    Ranks of direct sums of nonzero spaces are at least the number of summands.

    theorem LargeIndecomposable.Bricks.rigidFamily {k : Type u} [Field k] [Infinite k] (X : Type u) [Infinite X] :
    ∃ (T : Set X → Statement.Kron k), (∀ (b : Set X), Module.rank k ↑(T b).V = Cardinal.mk X ∧ Module.rank k ↑(T b).W = Cardinal.mk X ∧ Kron.ABInj (T b) ∧ (ModuleCat.Hom.hom (T b).a).range ⊔ (ModuleCat.Hom.hom (T b).b).range = ⊤) ∧ (∀ (b c : Set X), b ⊆ c → Nonempty ((T b ⟶ T c) ≃ₗ[k] k)) ∧ (∀ (b c : Set X), ¬b ⊆ c → ∀ (f : T b ⟶ T c), f = 0) ∧ (∀ (b : Set X), Nonempty (CategoryTheory.End (T b) ≃ₐ[k] k)) ∧ ∀ (b : Set X), IsBrickKron (T b)

    Theorem 5.6 (Göbel–Simson, Theorem 1.2(i),(iii) and Theorem 3.3), for infinite fields: a family of Kronecker modules T_β, β ⊆ X, with Hom(T_β, T_γ) ≅ k exactly when β ⊆ γ.
